Render / drawing comparison

Does the model look like what the contractor drew?

Twelve views rendered from designs/contractor-as-drawn.json, checked frame by frame against the five sheets they were modelled from. Ten findings below: what matches, what the tool can't draw, and what the drawings themselves never specify.

01 — Where it matches

01Ground-floor room order
Match
DrawingMẶT BẰNG TẦNG 1

Renderkhach view

The living room sits between the garage and the stair core, matching the sheet. This is a correction, not a carry-over: the first modelling pass had living and kitchen on the wrong sides of the core entirely.

02 — Where the render departs from the drawing

05The front facade has no glazing
Departure
DrawingMẶT ĐỨNG CHÍNH
Full-width window and door bands on five of seven levels, a louvred screen at tầng 2, recessed loggia above the entry.
Renderexterior_front view
One door at ground level. No window is visible on any of the seven storeys above it.

This is the single biggest visual gap between the two, and it isn't a modelling omission — the spec does author a door and a 1400mm window on every front bedroom's wall to its balcony (designs/contractor-as-drawn.json, e.g. ["ngu_truoc_f2","ban_cong_f2"]).

The renderer builds a full-height wall on every balcony edge regardless of the room type, and the auto-parapet feature only adds a railing on top of that wall — it never removes it. So every balcony and terrace in this model compiles correctly and renders as a sealed box. The glazing exists in the geometry; the wall in front of it just isn't supposed to be there. This is a pipeline behaviour (src/homedesign/blender/build_scene.py), not specific to this design — the same thing happens to tubehouse-dream's balconies.

06Balconies and terraces render enclosed, not open
Departure
DrawingMẶT BẰNG MÁI
SÂN THƯỢNG front and rear both hatched — the drawing's own convention for "no roof, open to sky."
Rendersan_thuong view
A closed room with a door. No railing, no open edge, no sky.

Same root cause as finding 05. Every balcony-typed room in the spec — both ban_công rows and both sân thượng zones — is geometrically correct and renders sealed for the same reason.

07The light well is wider than what's glazed
Departure
DrawingMẶT BẰNG MÁI, roof detail
Ô kính lấy sáng — a ~1700mm glazed insert sits within a larger, unglazed roof slab over the stair.
Rendergieng_troi view
Corridor beside the stair, lit from an opening overhead.

Deliberate, not an oversight. The renderer has no glass material, so a roof slab modelled solid over the stair — as literally drawn — turns the whole shaft into an unlit slot in every render that looks toward it.

The model instead punches the roof void over the stairwell's entire footprint (3005×4000mm) rather than the drawing's narrower glazed rectangle, trading literal geometry for a truthful picture: light actually reaches the stair. The render shows more open sky above the core than the glazing would really let through.

08The mezzanine's open void is filled with a placeholder floor
Departure
DrawingMẶT BẰNG LỬNG
The zone over the garage and living room is cross-hatched — no slab, open two storeys down.
Renderno view frames this zone
no camera looks at this room —
none of the 12 views is positioned here
The gallery has no shot of the placeholder itself.

The drawing's own hatch convention marks this as a genuine double-height opening — the reason a family room upstairs would look down into the entry below. The model leaves the footprint untiled on level 1 to match it.

But the pipeline's structural check requires every room on the floor above to be ≥80% covered by a room on the floor directly below, and can't represent a beam-spanned opening. A room named "SÀN GIẢ (Ô THÔNG TẦNG THEO BẢN VẼ)" — false floor, the double-height opening per the drawing — fills the gap on level 1 only so the model compiles. It carries no furniture and appears in no rendered view; it exists to satisfy the checker, not to depict anything. The real building has an open, light-filled stair-side void here; this model has an enclosed mezzanine floor instead.

09The stair core is 800mm deeper than drawn
Departure
FigureDrawnModelled
Stair-core run depth3200mm4000mm
Risers at H=3800mm21 (undimensioned)22 @ 172.7mm
Compensated byRear yard (sân sau) compressed 2000mm → 1200mm; plot depth stays 25000mm as drawn

A U-return flight sized to the Blondel relation at this storey's 3800mm floor-to-floor needs at least 3998.5mm of run for the drawn 3005mm-wide shaft — the drawn 3200mm does not fit. This is the same finding the 2026-08-12 drawing review raised independently from the 2D sheets alone: a shaft that cannot hold a compliant flight at the drawn dimensions is a real defect in the issued drawings, not a modelling artefact.

03 — What the drawings don't say

10No floor plan labels a lift shaft
Uncertain
DrawingMẶT BẰNG MÁI (roof only)
"Ô KỸ THUẬT THANG MÁY," 1950×2000mm — the only place the word "thang máy" appears on any sheet.
Renderexterior_aerial view
The roofed core, with the light-well void visible at its centre.

All three residential floor-plan sheets show the stair block followed by an unlabelled walled void, then the light well, then a WC — never a shaft marked "THANG MÁY." The label appears exactly once, on the roof plan, describing a plant room standing 2000mm above the roof slab.

The model infers a 2000×1800mm shaft stacking through all seven levels, sized from that single roof label — not measured from any floor plan, because none shows one. Two readings are equally consistent with what's drawn: the shaft runs the full height and the floor sheets simply omit a repeated label, or there is no passenger lift below roof level and the plant room describes a reserved future installation. This should be confirmed with the contractor before either reading is treated as fact — including in the separate lift-cost research this repo already produced, which assumed a shaft exists.

Findings 05–09 are recorded in full, with additional detail not repeated here, in designs/contractor-as-drawn.fidelity.md. Dimension provenance — which figure came from which sheet, and which were read directly versus reconstructed — is in designs/contractor-as-drawn.measurements.md. Neither the skewed ~7.2° site boundary, the rear-setback crossing, nor the permitted-height question from the 2026-08-12 drawing review are re-examined here; none of them are things a render could confirm or refute.
